on.s: Gestumblindi hét einn ríkr maðr í Reiðgotalandi. Hann var í óblíðu Heiðreks konungs. Í konungs hirð váru þeir sjau menn, er dæma skyldu öll mál manna þar í landi. Heiðrekr konungr blótaði Frey. Þann gölt, er mestan fekk, skyldi hann gefa Frey. Kölluðu þeir hann svá helgan, at yfir hans burst skyldi sverja um öll stór mál, ok skyldi þeim gelti blóta at sónarblóti. Jólaftan skyldi leiða sónargöltinn í höll fyrir konung, ok lögðu menn þá hendr yfir burst hans ok strengja heit. Heiðrekr konungr strengði þess heit, at engi maðr skyldi svá mikit hafa af gert við hann, ef á vald hans kæmi, at eigi skyldi kost eiga at hafa dóm spekinga hans. Sá skyldi ok friðheilagr vera fyrir honum, ef hann bæri upp gátur þær, er konungr kynni eigi ór at leysa. En er menn freistuðu at bera upp gátur fyrir honum, þá varð engi sú upp borin, er hann réði eigi. Konungr sendi orð Gestumblinda, at hann kæmi til hans, ok setti honum dag, ella sagðist konungr mundu láta koma til hans. Honum þótti hvárgi góðr kostrinn, því at hann vissi sik vanfæran at skipta orðum við konung. Honum þótti ok sín ván eigi góð, ef hann yrði at hafa dóm spekinganna, því at sakir váru nógar. Veit hann ok, ef konungs menn koma til hans, at þat kostar líf hans. Síðan blótaði hann Óðin ok bað hann fulltings ok hét honum stórum gjöfum. Eitt kveld kom gestr til Gestumblinda. Hann nefndist Gestumblindi. Þeir váru svá líkir, at hvárgan kenndi fyrir annan. Þeir skiptu klæðum, ok fór bóndi at hirða sik, en allir hugðu þar vera bónda, er gestrinn var. Þessi maðr ferr á konungs fund ok heilsar honum. Konungr sá við honum ok þagði. Gestumblindi mælti: "Því em ek hér kominn, herra, at ek vil sættast við yðr." Konungr spurði: "Viltu hafa dóm spekinga?" Gestumblindi mælti: "Eru engar fleiri undanlausnir?" Konungr segir: "Bera máttu upp gátur. Skaltu lauss, ef ek sé eigi." Gestumblindi svarar: "Lítt em ek þar til færr, en harðr er á annat borð." Konungr mælti: "Viltu heldr dóminn?" "Nei" segir hann, "heldr vil ek bera gáturnar upp." Konungr mælti: "Þat er ok rétt, en mikit liggr á. Sigrar þú mik, þá skaltu eiga dóttur mína, ok á þér eigi þess at varna. En ólíkr ertu til mikillar speki, en aldri varð þat enn, at ek sá eigi gátur þær, er fyrir mik váru upp bornar." Var síðan stóll settr undir Gestumblinda, ok hugðu menn gott til at heyra þar vitrlig orð. Þá mælti Gestumblindi:

Konungur spurði: "Viltu hafa dóm spekinga?" Gestumblindi mælti: "Eru engar fleiri undanlausnir?" Konungur segir: "Bera máttu upp gátur. Skaltu laus, ef eg sé eigi." en.s: There was a powerful man named Gestumblindi in Reiðgotaland. He was out of favour with King Heiðrekr. In the king's retinue there were seven men who were to judge all the cases of men in that land. King Heiðrekr sacrificed to Freyr. The largest boar he could get he was to give to Freyr. They held it so holy that over its bristles oaths were to be sworn in all great matters, and that boar was to be sacrificed at the atonement-sacrifice [sónarblót]. On Yule eve the atonement-boar was to be led into the hall before the king, and men then laid their hands on its bristles and made solemn vows. King Heiðrekr made the vow that no man should have done so much against him, if he came into his power, that he should not have the choice of receiving the judgement of his wise men. That man should also be inviolate before him if he put forward riddles which the king could not solve. But when men tried putting riddles to him, none was put forward that he did not solve. The king sent word to Gestumblindi that he should come to him, and set him a day; otherwise, the king said, he would have men come to him. Neither choice seemed good to him, because he knew himself ill-equipped to exchange words with the king. Nor did his prospects seem good if he had to take the judgement of the wise men, for the charges were many. He knows too that if the king's men come to him, it will cost him his life. Then he sacrificed to Óðinn and asked him for help and promised him great gifts. One evening a guest came to Gestumblindi. He called himself Gestumblindi. They were so alike that neither could be told from the other. They exchanged clothes, and the farmer went to hide himself, and everyone thought the farmer was there where the guest was. This man goes to meet the king and greets him. The king looked at him and was silent. Gestumblindi said: "I have come here, lord, because I want to be reconciled with you." The king asked: "Will you have the judgement of the wise men?" Gestumblindi said: "Are there no other ways out?" The king says: "You may put forward riddles. You shall be free if I do not see through them." Gestumblindi answers: "I am little fit for that, but the other course is hard." The king said: "Would you rather have the judgement?" "No," he says, "I would rather put forward the riddles." The king said: "That is also right, but much is at stake. If you defeat me, you shall have my daughter, and you shall not be refused that. But you seem unlikely to have great wisdom, and it has never yet happened that I did not see through the riddles that were put to me." Then a chair was set beneath Gestumblindi, and people looked forward to hearing wise words there. Then Gestumblindi said:

But if you are that Gestumblindi whom I took you for, then you are wiser than I supposed, for I had heard that your words were unwise, but now they are becoming wise." "It is likely that I shall soon run dry," says Gestumblindi, "but still I would like you to listen further:

en.s: That is an anchor with a thick and strong cable. It governs many a ship. It grips the earth with one of its flukes, and that one faces towards Hel; it saves many a man. But I greatly wonder at your skill with words and your wisdom." Gestumblindi said: "I am now nearly run out of riddles, but everyone is eager for his life.

en.s: That is a dung-beetle, and much is now being scraped together, when dung-beetles are the questions of powerful men." Gestumblindi answers: "Delays are the best of evils, but many a man wants to search further, and so some overlook things. I see now too that I must seek every way out.

en.s: There you saw a sow, and in her were nine piglets." Then the king had the sow killed, and in her were nine piglets, as Gestumblindi had said. Then the king said: "I do not know now but that wise men may have a hand in this, and I do not know what kind of man you are." Gestumblindi answers: "I am such as you can see, and I would gladly be granted my life and be free of these trials." The king answers: "You shall put forward riddles until you run out of them, or I fail to solve them." Gestumblindi said:

l: That is an arrow," says the king.

en.s: Then the king answers: "My retainers shall solve this riddle." They guessed many things, and none very seemly. Then the king said, when he saw that they were getting nowhere: "That horse you speak of is a linen loom, and its mare the weaving-sword, which is to shake the web up and down." Gestumblindi said:

on.s: Konungr brá þá Tyrfingi ok hjó til Gestumblinda, en hann brást í vals líki ok fló út gegnum hallarglugg einn. En sverðit kom á vélit valsins, ok er hann því vélstuttr jafnan síðan, svá sem heiðnir menn trúa. Ok var nú Óðinn honum reiðr orðinn, síðan hann hjó til hans, ok á þeiri nótt var konungr drepinn.

is.s: Konungur brá þá Tyrfingi og hjó til Gestumblinda, en hann brást í vals líki og fló út gegnum hallarglugg einn. En sverðið kom á vélið valsins, og er hann því vélstuttur jafnan síðan, svo sem heiðnir menn trúa. Og var nú Óðinn honum reiður orðinn, síðan hann hjó til hans, og á þeirri nótt var konungur drepinn.

en.s: Then the king drew Tyrfingr and struck at Gestumblindi, but he changed into the shape of a falcon and flew out through one of the hall's windows. But the sword struck the falcon's tail feathers, and that is why it has always been short-tailed since, as heathen men believe. And now Óðinn had become angry with him, because he had struck at him, and that same night the king was killed.
